# Survey Crops modelling choices

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_assumptions_doc.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Where no source gave a number, the team chose one. They are listed here so they can be checked. Main choices are re-run with other values (sensitivity runs); the results are in `docs/results/risk_calendar.md`.

## Risk calendar (`ASSUMPTIONS` in `src/compute/risk_calendar.py`)

| Name | Value | What it means | Why it is reasonable | Sensitivity run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flowering_window_days` | 7 | Heat at flowering/anthesis is counted over a window of this many days centred on the flowering date. | Flowering is not one day; a week around the flowering date is a plain, short window. A longer 15-day window is run as a check. | Yes: re-run with `15` |
| `hot_days` | 3 | A season is a 'problem year' for a heat/cold hazard when at least this many days in the sensitive stage cross the cited threshold. | One hot day rarely ruins a crop, so a few days are required. Fewer (1) and more (5) days are run as a check. | Yes: re-run with `1`, `5` |
| `threshold_end` | onset | When a threshold is cited as a range (e.g. mustard 25-29 C, potato night 20-25 C) the onset end is used; the severe end is a sensitivity run. | The onset end of a cited range is the earlier, more careful warning point. The severe end is run as a check. | Yes: re-run with `severe` |
| `waterlog_window_days` | 30 | Waterlogging is checked in the first this-many days after sowing (from the task spec, not a source). | Young seedlings are the most exposed to standing water, so only the first month after sowing is checked. No sensitivity run exists. | No |
| `saturated_day` | Dr = 0 and deep percolation > 0 | A 'saturated' day in the FAO-56 balance: the root zone is at field capacity and surplus water is draining that day (the balance has no runoff term, so this includes water that would pond or run off). | It is the simplest daily test that follows from the water balance already used, and it needs no extra data. | No |
| `turnaround_days` | 7 | Days between harvesting the previous crop and sowing the next one. | A short gap for harvesting, threshing and preparing land. No sensitivity run exists. | No |
| `combine_sources` | mean of per-source midpoints | When several kept rows cite a stage duration or threshold, each source's midpoint is taken and the mean of those is used; the full range is shown. | Taking one midpoint per source stops a source with many rows from outweighing the others; the full range stays visible. | No |
| `gdd_no_upper_cap` | none | GDD uses no upper temperature cap (none is cited). | Adding a cap would need a number that no kept source gives, so none is used. | No |
| `potato_main_season_window` | 11-01 to 11-30 | Potato has three cited BARC windows. The North (Nov 1-7) and South (Nov 17-30) main-season windows are merged; the early-variety window (Sep 24-Oct 7) is excluded because its notes say it is a separate sub-type. | The two cited main-season windows are kept; the early-variety window is a different sub-type, so it is not mixed in. | No |
| `boro_transplant_window_start` | earliest seedbed_start + shortest seedling_age | No kept row gives a boro transplanting window start, so it is derived from two cited values: the earliest seedbed sowing date plus the shortest seedling age. Boro 'sowing date' in this calendar means TRANSPLANTING date. | It uses only two cited numbers and invents none; it is a derived start, not a measured one. | No |
| `night_temperature` | POWER T2M_MIN | The daily minimum 2 m temperature stands in for night temperature. | The daily minimum is the coolest reading of the day, which is the closest NASA POWER variable to night temperature. | No |
| `water_season_length` | kc_table stage lengths | The water balance runs over the FAO-56 stage lengths in kc_table.csv (e.g. wheat 120 d), which differ from the cited maturity days. | The FAO-56 stage lengths are the ones the crop coefficients (Kc) were published for, so they stay consistent with each other. | No |
| `paddy_refill` | refill to ponding depth when the water layer is used up | Boro paddy: after land preparation the field holds the cited ponding depth; each day rain adds and ETc + percolation remove water; water above the ponding depth spills; when the layer would go below zero it is refilled to the ponding depth (counted as irrigation). Season = kc_table rice stage lengths (150 d), from transplanting. | It keeps the paddy water layer at the cited ponding depth and counts every top-up as irrigation, which is how a farmer manages a boro field. | No |
| `irrigation_event_count` | one watering = one day the FAO-56 balance refills the root zone; paddy: land preparation + each pond top-up | Waterings per season are counted from the same FAO-56 balance that gives irrigation_mm: each day it adds irrigation counts as one watering. For boro paddy the land-preparation flooding counts as one watering and every later pond top-up as one more. | It turns the irrigation depth already computed into a number a farmer can compare with how many times they can bring water. Pump capacity is not modelled, so it is a count, not a volume per watering. | No |
| `paddy_percolation_class` | clay if clay_pct >= 40 | Percolation uses the cited clay rate when SoilGrids clay >= 40% (USDA clay class lower bound), otherwise the cited loam rate. | The 40% clay line is the lower bound of the USDA clay class, so the cited clay and loam rates are applied by a published rule. | No |

## API (`API_ASSUMPTIONS` in `app.py`)

| Name | Value | What it means | Why it is reasonable | Sensitivity run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dswx_scene_lead_days` | 7days | DSWx-S1 scenes up to this many days before the flood date are used (a pass rarely falls on the exact flood day). | Radar passes come every few days, so a scene a week before the flood still shows the water that was already there. | No |
| `dswx_peak_max_lag_days` | 30days | If the largest DSWx-S1 flood-water reading comes more than this many days after the flood date, it is not this flood (e.g. Noakhali's December peak), so the water signal is reported as inconclusive and only SMAP is used. | A peak a month or more after the flood is more likely a different event, and calling it 'inconclusive' is safer than guessing. | No |
| `dswx_dry_floor` | median flood_fraction, 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31 | Water the method sees with no flood (wet paddies, ponds, radar speckle). 'Water mostly gone' = 90% of the water above this floor has drained (docs/results/post_flood.md). | Using the dry-season median (Jan-Mar 2025) as the floor means permanent water and speckle are not counted as flood. | No |
| `district_max_distance_km` | 60km | A GPS point (lat, lon) is served by the nearest of the 5 district points (data/processed/district_metadata.csv) only if it lies within this distance; farther points get DISTRICT_NOT_COVERED. | The data are for the area around a district point, so a point far from every district would get numbers that do not describe it. | No |
| `twin_rain_week_mm` | 20mm/week | In the field-twin replay a week is flagged 'rain' when IMERG rain that week is at least this much (for the animation only; not a risk rule). | It only picks which weeks of the animation show a rain icon; it feeds no risk number or ranking. | No |
